ov: Nocturnal freshwater fish of South America that stun prey with electric shocks. They must breathe air, have poor eyesight and find their way by electrolocation. They mainly eat fish.

why.dg: Its shocks reach 860 volts, strong enough to drive off animals as large as horses.
why.ac: Nocturnal, with poor eyesight made up for by sensing electric fields.

fx: Studies of electric eels in the 1770s helped lead to the invention of the battery in 1800.
notes: Group entry (three species since 2019). The existing fact is confirmed: up to 860 volts, and a knifefish, not a true eel.
